title: 搭讪自然的重要性

timeline.summary: A man compliments a woman, introduces himself and asks whether she is visiting or local.

She asks whether someone is filming. The exchange includes a denial followed by the statement that they plan to shoot material but have not started, although the published camera is already recording.
He proposes coffee at a later opportunity; both mention current commitments, discuss tomorrow/the day after, and move toward a WeChat request.
They discuss age. The transcript contains an 18-year-old estimate and broad statements about Chinese women's makeup making ages difficult to judge.
They discuss how long she will stay in Chengdu; he asks her to stay longer and give him a chance, followed by brief assent and goodbye.
No reliable ASR; ending does not establish later contact or a date.

claims.speaker: field participants, turns partly uncertain
claims.statement: The woman asks whether filming is occurring; the man says they intend to film material but have not started.
claims.conditions: The camera was already capturing the interaction. This cannot be treated as informed recording or publication consent.

claims.speaker: field participants, turns partly uncertain
claims.statement: A coffee invitation is shifted away from the current day after both mention other commitments, followed by a WeChat request.
claims.conditions: Rescheduling and short assent do not prove voluntary contact exchange or a future meeting; refusal and uncertainty must remain easy.

claims.speaker: field participants, turns partly uncertain
claims.statement: The exchange includes an estimate of age 18 and continues into appearance-based age discussion.
claims.conditions: Adulthood is not verified. Appearance, makeup or student status must never substitute for confirming that a person is an adult before romantic pursuit.

claims.speaker: field man
claims.statement: He asks her to stay longer in Chengdu and give him a chance.
claims.conditions: An emotional request is not consent evidence and should not pressure travel, schedule, contact or romantic decisions.

examples.summary: One continuous public interaction includes a filming question, tentative rescheduling, a contact request, ambiguous age talk and an emotional request; none establishes informed publication consent or later outcome.

speaker_attribution.speaker: field man
speaker_attribution.basis: Visible male participant; formal source did not independently prove he is Mikey, so claims remain role-attributed.

speaker_attribution.speaker: approached woman
speaker_attribution.basis: White-jacketed participant visible in both frames; exact short turns and age statement are not independently diarized.

visual_findings: Both sampled frames show the same man and woman in a single public location beside an advertising panel; no case change is visible.
Frame 000001 carries a subtitle saying filming has not started while the interaction is visibly being recorded, creating a direct transparency and consent concern.
Both participants use phones, but screens are unreadable and do not prove contact saving. Faces, bodies, location and bystanders remain visible.

permissions.reason: Duplicate formal source with blocking recording-consent and adulthood uncertainty, plus privacy, pressure and unverified contact/outcome issues.

limitations: Automatic transcript was not word-for-word audio checked or diarized.
Two sparse frames do not equal continuous audio-visual review.
The participant's age/adulthood, informed filming/publication consent, contact exchange and later outcome are unverified.
Visible phone use does not prove voluntary contact saving.
